rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the largest uncertainty is whether a simple unimodal baseline is competitive. config_001 tests a low-complexity RNA-only single-profile model using PCA, providing a clean reference without aggregation or fusion. It will establish a performance anchor and reduce uncertainty about the RNA representation baseline, making later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion more interpretable under a limited budget.

The only completed experiment is a modest RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, with validation accuracy 0.485 and F1 0.464, so there is still no evidence on whether image features are informative. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the key modality/representation question while keeping profile setting and aggregation simple. This is the best next use of budget because it establishes whether image data can compete with RNA before investing further in multimodal fusion, multiprofile aggregation, or more expensive image encoders.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only single-profile PCA (config_001, accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (config_010, accuracy 0.208, F1 0.172), so the RNA branch is the most promising direction to exploit. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile modeling with simple aggregation improves over the single-profile RNA baseline. config_002 tests this with the same PCA RNA encoder and adds only multiprofile plus avgpool, the simplest necessary aggregation. This is a minimal logical extension that reduces uncertainty about profile setting and aggregation before investing in more complex encoders, transformer aggregation, or multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is rna_only with multiprofile, pca_n2000, and avgpool (acc 0.5907, F1 0.5727), clearly better than singleprofile PCA RNA (acc 0.4849). This suggests multiprofile aggregation is important, but it is not yet known whether transformer aggregation improves over simple avgpool. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the promising RNA-only multiprofile PCA setting, so it cleanly isolates the aggregation decision. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest current direction while reducing uncertainty about a key design choice before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

RNA PCA multiprofile with avgpool is currently the strongest result (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), while image-only ResNet singleprofile is weak (accuracy 0.208, F1 0.172). The key uncertainty is whether the image modality has useful signal under the same multiprofile avgpool setting that helped RNA, or whether the profile/aggregation gain is RNA-specific. config_011 tests image-only ResNet with multiprofile and avgpool, isolating the modality effect against config_002 and the profile/aggregation effect against config_010 without introducing fusion. This is the best next experiment because it establishes whether image features are worth combining before spending limited budget on multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest setting so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), outperforming single-profile PCA and multiprofile transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet models are much weaker. This experiment tests whether replacing PCA with a learned nonlinear RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improves that best RNA-only setting, isolating the effect of RNA representation while keeping profile setting and aggregation fixed. It is the best next step because it exploits the most promising current direction with a controlled single-factor change, reduces uncertainty about RNA representation, and will inform whether learned RNA encoders should be used in later multimodal comparisons.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile avgpool with scvi_n200 is the strongest configuration so far (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), multiprofile avgpool outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation for PCA, and image-only models are much weaker. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the scgpt RNA representation can improve over scvi_n200 under the same best profile and aggregation settings. This experiment tests that by changing only the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest RNA-only direction, isolates the representation effect, and can either find a better encoder or confirm scvi_n200 before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA multiprofile avgpool with scvi_n200 is the strongest setting so far, while image-only resnet50 is weak even with multiprofile avgpool. The key uncertainty is whether image performance is limited by the resnet50 representation or by the image modality itself. config_014 tests an image-only ViT with the same multiprofile avgpool setting as config_011, cleanly isolating the effect of image encoder representation. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about whether a stronger image encoder could make image features useful before investing budget in multimodal fusion configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models dominate image-only models, and scvi_n200 with avgpool is the strongest configuration so far (0.650 accuracy / 0.628 F1). Transformer aggregation was worse than avgpool for PCA, but its effect with the stronger scvi representation is still unknown. config_006 tests only aggregation while keeping the best RNA encoder and multiprofile setting, cleanly isolating whether transformer aggregation can improve the top RNA representation. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces key uncertainty about aggregation before adding multimodal fusion or testing weaker image-based directions.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is the strongest simple baseline (0.650 acc), and image-only multiprofile imagenet_vit_l with avgpool is the best image baseline so far (0.332 acc), though both image settings are weak. This tests whether adding the best image representation to the best RNA representation improves validation accuracy over the RNA-only model, using the same profile and aggregation settings and a simple concat fusion baseline. It is the most informative next step because it directly evaluates the value of multimodal fusion before spending budget on more complex fusion, transformer aggregation, or weaker image encoders.
